clue.text: An unctuous individual possibly agrees with the right

indicators.note: possibly suggests the letters of the word agrees could be arranged some other way

parts.note: R is the standard abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A smarmy person goes along with the political right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' is the anagram signal; 'right' is the single-letter abbreviation, not a political side.
explanation.definitionFit: A greaser is a slang term for a fawning, oily flatterer, someone unctuous in manner.

clue.text: Old king — a scoffer, and more influential

parts.note: GR stands for Georgius Rex, King George, a monarch of the past
someone who scoffs food greedily is an eater

explanation.surface: An ancient monarch, mocking and powerful, carries more weight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scoffer' suggests someone who mocks, but here it is someone who scoffs, that is wolfs down, food.
explanation.definitionFit: Greater is the comparative of great, so it means having more importance or sway.

clue.text: Squeezed out, so it's said

definitions.meaning: juice pressed from fruit has been squeezed out
a thought put into words has been stated

explanation.definitionFit: Juice can be pressed out of fruit, and an opinion can be voiced; the one verb covers both.

clue.text: Cattle fodder in Northern Europe

definitions.meaning: a root vegetable, a large turnip, fed to livestock
a native of ... lives in Northern Europe

explanation.surface: Livestock feed from Scandinavia.
explanation.definitionFit: The swede is a turnip-like root grown for animal feed, and a Swede is a person from Sweden.

clue.text: Military personnel authorise surrender

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps
to sign a document authorises it

explanation.surface: Soldiers approve a capitulation.
explanation.definitionFit: To give up a post or concede a game is to surrender it.

clue.text: Money invested in London?

definitions.meaning: funds put into a business are its stock of wealth
London is the chief city of the United Kingdom, its seat of government

explanation.surface: Funds placed in the city of London.
explanation.definitionFit: Capital is the wealth used to run a business, and the chief city of a country, as London is of Britain.

clue.text: Force might affect one's view of things

definitions.meaning: in northern England a force is a waterfall

definitions.text: might affect one's view of things
definitions.meaning: an eye condition clouds the lens and blurs sight

explanation.surface: Power can colour how someone sees the world.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Force' looks like power or strength, but in the north of England a force is a waterfall.
explanation.definitionFit: A cataract is a large waterfall, and also a clouding of the eye's lens that impairs vision.

clue.text: How surprising, to prefer a bore!

indicators.note: an exclamation of surprise suggests the letters to prefer a are startled into a new order

explanation.surface: Fancy choosing a tedious person over someone else!
explanation.walkthrough: 'bore' reads as a dull person, but it is a verb: to drill a hole. 'How surprising' shuffles TO PREFER A.
explanation.definitionFit: To perforate is to pierce holes through something, as a drill bores.

clue.text: Use a comb and cause some irritation

definitions.meaning: backcombing hair or carding wool raises the fibres
to taunt someone playfully annoys them

explanation.surface: Combing hair can be annoying.
explanation.definitionFit: To tease is to fluff up hair or wool with a comb, and to provoke someone mildly.

clue.text: Following a row a note must be written as ruled

indicators.note: the remaining pieces come after the row in the answer

parts.note: a line is a row of things
TE is a note in tonic sol-fa, also spelt ti

explanation.surface: After a line, a musical note should be written down as instructed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ruled' sounds like governed, but it means marked with lines, like ruled paper.
explanation.definitionFit: Lineate describes something marked with lines, as paper is ruled for writing.

clue.text: The queen seems worried about public relations

indicators.note: the shuffled letters go around the abbreviation for public relations
worried suggests the word seems is agitated into another arrangement

explanation.surface: The monarch appears anxious about her press coverage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worried' makes EMESS from the fodder, and 'about' wraps those letters around the abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: An empress is a female sovereign ruling an empire, a queen in rank.

clue.text: Coaches without hesitation giving ground

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside: the coaches enclose the hesitation

parts.note: a train is a string of railway coaches
er is the sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: Sports trainers who speak without faltering hand over territory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like 'minus', but here it carries its old sense of outside, so the hesitation sits inside the coaches.
explanation.definitionFit: Terrain is a stretch of land considered for its physical features.

clue.text: Poor man's entertainment?

parts.note: read as a show belonging to a pauper, it names John Gay's 1728 ballad opera

explanation.definitionFit: Gay's ballad opera takes its title from a mendicant, a poor man, and is a stage entertainment.

clue.text: Approaching the age of rebellion

definitions.meaning: a child described as '... five' is about to turn five

explanation.surface: Teenagers nearing the age of revolt.
explanation.definitionFit: Rising before an age means nearly reaching it, and a rising is a revolt or insurrection.

clue.text: Managed to overturn the salt when telling the tale

indicators.note: the word for managed is turned over, read in reverse

parts.note: to run a business is to manage it, past tense ran
a salt is an old sailor; a rating is a naval sailor below officer rank

explanation.surface: Someone tipped over the salt cellar while telling a story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to overturn' reverses RAN to NAR. 'the salt' is not table salt but a seafarer.
explanation.definitionFit: Narrating means recounting a story, telling the tale.

clue.text: To wit, the mob would appear game

parts.note: SC abbreviates scilicet, Latin for namely or to wit
a rabble is a disorderly crowd or mob

explanation.surface: Namely, the crowd would look sporting.
explanation.walkthrough: SC, from Latin scilicet, means 'that is to say' in old texts and footnotes.
explanation.definitionFit: Scrabble is a board game of building words from letter tiles.

clue.text: The warder who's not a vegetarian

definitions.meaning: a Yeoman Warder guards the Tower of London
someone who eats beef is no vegetarian

explanation.surface: A prison guard who eats meat.
explanation.walkthrough: Beefeaters are the ceremonial guards of the Tower of London, officially Yeoman Warders.
explanation.definitionFit: Tower guards are nicknamed for their supposed beef rations, and literally one who eats beef is a meat-eater.

clue.text: Fit means used, that's quite clear

indicators.note: used in the sense of worked over, the letters of fit means are put to a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Suitable methods have been employed, which is obvious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'used' signals that FIT MEANS is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Manifest means plainly evident, obvious to the eye or mind.

clue.text: Going for French and German articles on fashion

parts.note: un is the French indefinite article
der is a German definite article
a way of doing something is its fashion or manner

explanation.surface: Heading off for items about style from French and German magazines.
explanation.walkthrough: 'articles' are grammatical, not pieces in magazines.
explanation.definitionFit: A project in progress is under way, already going.

clue.text: Spoke of downright newspaper leader

parts.note: utter means complete, downright
ED is short for editor, the head of a newspaper

explanation.surface: Talked about a thoroughly bad newspaper editorial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'newspaper leader' suggests an editorial but means the editor, ED.
explanation.definitionFit: Uttered is the past tense of utter, to voice words: spoke.

clue.text: Deplore crack about exercise

indicators.note: the word for a crack goes around the exercise abbreviation

parts.note: a rent is a split or tear, a crack
PE is physical education, school exercise

explanation.surface: Lament a split over a workout.
explanation.definitionFit: To repent is to feel regret for, to deplore one's own actions.

clue.text: The sunburned man's touching line

parts.note: skin that is sunburnt has a tan
a gent is a man

explanation.surface: A suntanned fellow's poignant poem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'touching line' suggests moving poetry but is the geometric term.
explanation.definitionFit: In geometry a tangent is a straight line that touches a curve at one point.

clue.text: Nap raised by accident

parts.note: the nap of a fabric is its pile
something raised is up

explanation.surface: A doze interrupted by a crash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nap' reads as a short sleep, but it is the raised fibres on cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: A pile-up is a crash involving several vehicles.

clue.text: A great sheet of water turning into a nice patch of ice

indicators.note: turning into says the letters of a nice patch of ice change into another form

explanation.surface: A large expanse of water freezes into a pleasant ice patch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning into' reads as freezing but rearranges A NICE PATCH OF ICE.
explanation.definitionFit: The Pacific is the largest of the world's oceans, a vast body of water.

clue.text: Muse, if there's time to

parts.note: an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: Reflect, if there is a moment for it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Muse' looks like a verb, to ponder, but names one of the nine Muses of Greek myth.
explanation.definitionFit: Erato is the Greek Muse of lyric and love poetry.

clue.text: Odd route to take — most odd!

indicators.note: odd describes the word route made strange, its letters out of order

explanation.surface: Taking a strange path is very peculiar.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'Odd' rearranges ROUTE; 'most odd' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Outré means unconventional to the point of bizarre, extremely strange.

clue.text: Figure out a way to get cash for property

definitions.meaning: to grasp or work something out mentally
to sell assets and turn them into money

explanation.surface: Working out how to cash in on a house.
explanation.definitionFit: To realise is to come to understand, and also to convert assets into money by selling them.

clue.text: Among the adolescent it lends style

indicators.note: among signals that the letters sit inside the run adolescent it lends

explanation.surface: In teenagers it gives an air of fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'style' looks like fashion but is a verb: to give a title to.
explanation.definitionFit: To style someone is to name or designate them, which is to give them a title.

clue.text: A medical attendant has a duty to ensure dryness

parts.note: DR is short for doctor
ought expresses obligation, being duty-bound

explanation.surface: A doctor is obliged to keep a patient dry.
explanation.definitionFit: A drought is a long period without rain, extreme dryness.

clue.text: Single lapse admitted by dope, one time entertainer

indicators.note: admitted by puts the pieces inside the word for dope

parts.note: pot is slang for cannabis, dope
I is the Roman numeral one
to err is to lapse or make a mistake

explanation.surface: A drug user confesses a lone slip; once he was a performer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one time' means former: the white-faced clown of old French pantomime.
explanation.definitionFit: Pierrot is the sad clown of French pantomime, a stock stage entertainer of past centuries.
